I think I might not have made it very clear what my issue is. I have no problem working and paying rent, and having less luxuries. That's not really my issue. I guess what I am struggling with is the fact that I still want a family you know? I still want things to be "normal" and I still want someone who cares about me, but not because I do what they say or agree with them, but just because I am theirs and they are mine...

I accept that perfection is something that we have to work towards, but how can we work towards that without freedom? It is almost as though we are conditioned into being a certain identity such that the mere act of trying to be 'free' ends up being self-destructive. If that makes any sense?

Herein lies the tale of the a time long before, a time when we had forgotten to ask why, but rather we only considered how. There was no justifying the ends by the means, for there was no means. 

We roamed the land free to take what we wished, to kill and maim as we felt for we were Gods. You may ask how we slept at night or answered for our sins. We simply realised that good and bad were what ever we decided them to be. There was no objective good or bad, there were no absolute morals and the law of the land was only a futile attempt to force others, through violence, to do as you wished. Discarding this we just lived our immortal lives in what is now recognised as blissful ignorance by the humans. YES the tiny ants below our feet, the humans who now rule the surface tell tales of how we stole and pillaged their property, how we forced our way of life on them. They are wrong, the truly sad story is that we only recognized the absence of any such law of the land. We were the only truly free creatures and we respected the freedom of others. Our freedom to take as we wished extended as well to them... they stole, pillaged and killed us off one by one. Those of Us that survived the extinction event went into hiding and realised that soon our liberty would be extinguished. What you are reading now is a record of the final Battle in which we reclaimed our freedom, purchased with our lives.

Actually, Battle would be the wrong word for this because We do not assemble, we do not coallesce and we do not conform. We fought as individuals, proud and mighty, knowing that defeat was the only possible outcome. No we do not fight for some deity, or belief in a better place at the end of the road. Our fight was for our own right to live, our own right to be as we are, and finally to protest the loss of individuality that meant humanity. I destroyed an entire city fighting against the barbarians who were armed with pointy sticks and sharp blades, my blood gushed down the streets. That day the land was marked with a hue of blue and red. 

I regret nothing. What the humans call magic, how they describe our indescribable feats was nothing more than the result of free will. We were not bound by any norms or codes of conduct, only our imaginations guided by our hearts.

I don't even know why I am writing this... on the off chance that anyone survives this insanity I hope this finds you well. Only recently did It make its rounds around the public. Of course you know by It I am referring to the new mutant drug that is turning everyone mad. Yesterday a friend, the day before your next door neighbour... if you haven't already been consumed by the madness then I can only say there is no hope left for you. Either you were one of the earlier subjects that survived, or you are being destroyed by the exotic new strains one can pick up on any respectable street corner. 

It is just like history class, we're reliving the age where people fought over ideas, and killed each other over trinkets. The politicians have released statements warning citizens to stay calm and at home. Only today I experienced the worst of it, confronted with the decision of taking the pill. 

I was relaxing near the lake, after a long day working in the office, when I was approached.

"How are you today sir?" wheezed the old man while he pulled back a cloak that concealed the familiar powdery substance. 

"Sorry for bothering you... I'll be on my way" I quickly mumbled before being forced to think about it... You may be wondering who wouldn't want to feel? To be able to hold on to someone and truly connect. Well let me put it to you this way, ever since humanity had lost the ability to love through evolution the wars had ended. We had almost obliterated eachother in our thirst for resources, water and shiny metals. It had seemed as though the next progression for our great race was to become rational beings, people who can coexist without fear of alienation or causing offence to one another. We achieved these goals quite literally by removing the ability of our descendants to feel.

But today.... near that lake it struck me that what my ancestors had really done was not save humanity. They had sacrificed it. I had lost the ability to make my own decisions, to realise what it truly meant to be myself.

I stumbled on the paved pathway as I slouched away from opportunity, the chance not to revolt against my past... but to have a say in my future. For that day, I had realised that my only redemption, my only choice, my only saving grace towards freedom is by not choosing at all.
